description.value: The study examined changes in whole-brain functional connectivity following real-time fMRI neurofeedback training of the right inferior frontal cortex in adolescents with ADHD, and assessed specificity by comparison with ADHD adolescents trained on the left parahippocampal gyrus and by relating connectivity changes to clinical symptom changes.

design.value: A randomized controlled trial of fMRI neurofeedback in adolescents with ADHD, comparing right inferior frontal cortex neurofeedback with left parahippocampal gyrus control neurofeedback. Functional connectivity was compared between the first and last neurofeedback runs and between groups, with exploratory correlations to pre-post clinical changes.

description.value: Eighteen right-handed boys aged 12–17 years old with ADHD who received fMRI neurofeedback training of the right inferior frontal cortex.

inclusion_criteria.value: They all met the clinical DSM-5 criteria for the diagnosis of ADHD, combined hyperactive/impulsive and inattentive (N = 16) or inattentive (N = 2) subtypes.

exclusion_criteria.value: neurological or comorbid psychiatric disorders, except for disruptive behaviour disorder

diagnostic_instrument.value: Schedule of Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Age Children-Present and Lifetime version (K-SADS-PL)

clinical_characteristics.value: combined hyperactive/impulsive and inattentive (N = 16) or inattentive (N = 2) subtypes

medication_status.value: Fifteen boys received stable psychostimulant administration throughout the fMRI-Neurofeedback period: methylphenidate N = 13 and dexamphetamine N = 2. Three ceased taking medication for at least seven days before baseline testing.

description.value: Thirteen ADHD boys trained to enhance the left parahippocampal gyrus.

inclusion_criteria.value: meeting DSM-5 criteria for the diagnosis of ADHD, combined hyperactive/impulsive and inattentive (N = 11) or inattentive (N = 2) subtypes

exclusion_criteria.value: neurological or comorbid psychiatric disorders, except for disruptive behaviour disorder

recruitment_method.value: recruited and assessed in the same way

medication_status.value: Nine control boys received stable psychostimulant administration throughout the fMRI-Neurofeedback period: methylphenidate N = 9. Three ceased taking medication for at least seven days before baseline testing and one control boy was stimulant-naïve.

task_description.value: Boys were offered 14 fMRI-Neurofeedback runs in four scan visits over 2 weeks. Each run consisted of seven rest blocks and six activation blocks. During activation blocks, boys were asked to move a rocket towards space by any means they found helpful, receiving continuous feedback about BOLD activation in the target ROI.

instructions.value: You can try to concentrate on the rocket or try any other method that works for you.

stimuli.value: An underwater dolphin image during rest blocks and a video-clip of a rocket during activation blocks.

task_performance_measures.value: A score (0–10), reflecting the percentage of distance travelled through space during each run
percentage of distance travelled through space

instrument.value: 3T General Electric MR750 MRI scanner with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: fMRI-Neurofeedback scans were collected using an T2*-weighted gradient echo, echo-planar image sequence. The body coil was used for radiofrequency transmission. The sequence used 40 3-mm slices with a 0.3-mm slice gap, a 64 × 64 matrix, and a 21.1-cm FOV.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2*-weighted gradient echo, echo-planar image sequence

instrument.value: 3T General Electric MR750 MRI scanner with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: A T1-weighted structural scan, used as a structural localizer, was collected at the beginning of each scanning session.
fMRI data were first processed to minimise motion related artefacts. After realignment, data were smoothed using a Gaussian filter at 7.8 mm FWHM.

steps.value: Rigid body realignment to a template consisting of the average intensity at each voxel over the whole experiment
Transformation of functional connectivity maps to standard space by rigid body transformation and affine transformation onto a Talairach template

model_settings.value: Pre- and post-fMRI-Neurofeedback effects on clinical measures; effect size was calculated as Cohen's d.

estimator.value: Rubin's Rules for combining estimates from 20 multiply-imputed datasets

model_settings.value: For each seed region, the average time series over the whole ROI was used as a model for a whole-brain correlation analysis producing functional connectivity maps. Group connectivity maps were computed by determining the median correlation coefficient across subjects at each voxel.

estimator.value: median-based statistic and randomization-based voxel- and cluster-wise tests

model_settings.value: Functional connectivity differences between the last (11th or earlier) and first fMRI-Neurofeedback run, with run as within-group repeated measure and group as between-group measure for group comparisons.

estimator.value: randomization-based tests; voxel-level p < 0.05 followed by data-driven cluster-level thresholding to obtain less than one false-positive cluster per whole-brain map

model_settings.value: Two-tailed exploratory correlations between functional connectivity changes and changes in ADHD-RS and CPRS-R clinical measures.
